title: AMR surveillance network
tables: Public-health agencies, hospital networks, veterinary/environmental programs and research consortia.
AMR data can be delayed, non-standardized and difficult to compare across sites.
Validated local results; de-identification; Hive data model; quality filters; dashboards; governance and access control.
Sites generate reviewed results -> map to common schema -> remove/minimize identifiers -> run quality checks -> aggregate by organism/drug/location/time -> publish governed views.
Resistance trends, coverage/quality metrics, alerts for review and downloadable analysis datasets.
Digitization at the source can improve timeliness and provenance of surveillance data.
Surveillance does not equal outbreak prediction. Requires representative sampling, harmonized methods, deduplication, privacy, data-sharing agreements, bias analysis and public-health interpretation.
